q: A transaction of a depot cannot be taken to its final head immediately because a supporting debit is still awaited, so it is parked temporarily under the suspense grouping of the Government accounts. In the Government system of classification, Suspense Accounts are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Transactions that cannot yet be taken to their final head, pending an awaited debit or clearance, are parked under Suspense Accounts, Major Head 8658 in the Government classification.

q: The ordinary working expenses of Indian Railways - the revenue expenditure on working and maintenance - are brought to account in the Union accounts under Major Head:
e: Ordinary working expenses of Railways - revenue expenditure on working and maintenance - are brought to account under Major Head 3002 in the Union accounts.

q: A new line constructed by Indian Railways is a capital asset, and the outlay on it must appear under the capital head for Railways in the Union accounts, namely Major Head:
e: Capital outlay on Railways, such as construction of a new line, is accounted under Major Head 5002, the capital head for Railways in the Union accounts.

q: The interest payable by the Government of India on its market loans and other debt obligations is classified in the Government accounts under Major Head:
e: Interest payments on market loans and other debt obligations of the Government of India are classified under Major Head 2049, Interest Payments.

q: Pension and other retirement benefits payable to retired Government employees are classified in the Government accounts under Major Head:
e: Pensions and other retirement benefits of Government employees are classified under Major Head 2071, Pensions and Other Retirement Benefits.

q: A classification clerk must arrange the six tiers of Government account classification from the broadest to the most detailed. The tier that stands last, at the most detailed level, in the sequence Sector, Sub-Major Head, Major Head, Minor Head and Sub Head is:
e: The classification tiers run Sector, Sub-Major Head, Major Head, Minor Head, Sub Head and finally Detailed Head, which is the most detailed level of classification.

q: In the Appropriation Accounts of a grant, the excess or saving for the year is struck not against the amount originally budgeted, but against:

options.A: The Revised Estimates of the year
options.B: The Budget Estimates of the following year
options.C: The final grant or appropriation, after taking supplementary grants, re-appropriations and surrenders into account
options.D: The average expenditure of the preceding three years

e: In the Appropriation Accounts, excess or saving is struck against the final grant or appropriation - the original grant as modified by supplementary grants, re-appropriations and surrenders.

q: Audit finds that expenditure properly chargeable to one grant has been booked under a different head, so that it escapes being counted against the correct grant. Detecting exactly this kind of error is the concern of:

options.C: Internal audit by the Accounts Department
options.D: Appropriation audit, which verifies that expenditure is booked under the correct head against the proper grant or appropriation

e: Appropriation audit verifies that expenditure is booked under the correct head and charged against the proper grant or appropriation, so misclassification that escapes the correct grant is its concern.

q: Under the head of scrutiny described as audit against provision of funds, the audit office verifies that:

options.A: The sanction for the expenditure was issued by an authority competent to issue it
options.B: The expenditure does not exceed the grant or appropriation and has been incurred for the purpose for which the funds were provided
options.C: The orders governing the expenditure are consistent with the governing rules
options.D: The expenditure was incurred with due regard to wisdom and economy

e: Audit against provision of funds verifies only that expenditure does not exceed the grant or appropriation and is incurred for the purpose for which the funds were provided.

q: A sanction for a work is produced before audit, but it bears the signature of an officer who had no financial power to issue it. Examination of whether the sanction was issued by a competent authority and conforms to the applicable rules falls under:

options.C: Certification audit of the Finance Accounts

e: Audit against sanctions examines whether the sanction was issued by an authority competent to issue it and conforms to the applicable rules and orders, which is exactly the defect here.

q: Expenditure on a project is formally regular and duly sanctioned, yet audit brings it to notice as wasteful and lacking in faithfulness and economy. Audit scrutiny of this wider kind is known as:
e: Propriety audit judges expenditure by wisdom, faithfulness and economy, so formally regular and sanctioned spending can still be brought to notice as wasteful under it.

q: An audit study asks whether a programme delivered its intended results economically, efficiently and effectively, rather than merely whether the rules were followed. In ISSAI terms this is one of the three broad types of public-sector audit, the other two being financial audit and compliance audit. The study described is:

options.D: Performance audit, also described as Value-for-Money audit

e: A study of whether a programme delivered results economically, efficiently and effectively is performance audit, also called Value-for-Money audit, one of the three ISSAI audit types.

q: Before finalising a paragraph proposed for the CAG's Report, the audit office sends the draft to the Ministry concerned. This step is taken so that:

options.A: The paragraph can be voted upon by the Public Accounts Committee in advance
options.B: The facts stated in the paragraph are confirmed from the Ministry or department concerned and its comments are invited
options.C: The approval of the Finance Minister can be obtained for the paragraph
options.D: The paragraph can be published in the Gazette before the Report is laid

e: A Draft Para is sent to the Ministry or department concerned so that the facts stated are confirmed and its comments are invited before the paragraph is finalised for the CAG's Report.

q: After a local audit, only minor irregularities are noticed in a small office and they do not call for a detailed Inspection Report. Audit brings such minor irregularities to the notice of the executive through:

options.B: A Draft Para for the CAG's Report
options.C: An Audit Para in the Finance Accounts
options.D: An Action Taken Note to the Public Accounts Committee

e: Minor irregularities noticed in local audit that do not warrant a detailed Inspection Report are brought to the executive's notice through a Test Audit Note.

q: An Inspection Report issued after local audit of a unit contains, in its first part, the serious irregularities that require the attention of higher authorities. The Report is ordinarily divided into:

options.A: Part I for the Railway Board and Part II for the zonal Railway
options.B: Part I containing the accounts and Part II containing the replies of the executive
options.C: Part I containing serious irregularities requiring the attention of higher authorities, and Part II containing other, less serious irregularities
options.D: Part I for voted expenditure and Part II for charged expenditure

e: An Inspection Report is ordinarily in two parts: Part I contains serious irregularities requiring the attention of higher authorities, and Part II contains other, less serious irregularities.

q: The Government's Action Taken Notes on paragraphs in the CAG's Report are not sent straight to the Public Accounts Committee. Before being sent to the Committee, the Notes are:

options.A: Approved by the Railway Convention Committee
options.B: Certified by the FA&CAO of the Railway concerned
options.C: Placed before the Estimates Committee for its remarks

e: Government Action Taken Notes on CAG paragraphs are vetted by Audit before being sent to the Public Accounts Committee, so that the Committee receives a verified statement.

q: The audit that ends with the CAG's certificate on the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts of the Union is known as:
e: Certification audit, or financial attest audit, is the audit that ends with the CAG's certificate on the Finance Accounts and Appropriation Accounts; Q666 states the same point.

q:
Consider the following statements about a case where expenditure under a sub-head exceeds its provision, but savings under other sub-heads keep the total grant within its limit:
1. An Excess Grant must be voted by Parliament to regularise the excess under the sub-head.
2. Regularisation by Parliament through an Excess Grant is necessary only where the total amount of the grant or appropriation is exceeded.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Only statement 2 is correct: an Excess Grant is needed only where the total grant or appropriation is exceeded; an excess under one sub-head offset by savings elsewhere is regularised within the grant.

q: A zonal railway reports gross traffic earnings of Rs 7,000 crore. Its working expenses, inclusive of appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, amount to Rs 5,950 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway is:
e: Operating Ratio = working expenses divided by gross traffic earnings x 100 = 5950 / 7000 x 100 = 85 per cent.

q: For a year, the total expenditure of the Government of India is Rs 40,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 27,00,000 crore and its non-debt capital receipts, comprising recoveries of loans and disinvestment proceeds, are Rs 1,50,000 crore. The fiscal deficit for the year is:
e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts = 40,00,000 - (27,00,000 + 1,50,000) = Rs 11,50,000 crore.

q: A pay clerk credits the Provident Fund subscriptions recovered from staff salaries to the Consolidated Fund of India. The Accounts Officer objects that these moneys belong to a different part of the Government accounts, namely:

options.C: The Capital section of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Provident Fund subscriptions are public moneys held for subscribers and are credited to the Public Account of India, not to the Consolidated Fund, to which only revenues, loans and loan repayments go under Article 266(1).

q:
Consider the following statements about expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India:
1. It can be discussed in Parliament, though it is not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
2. Although not voted, it is still included in the Appropriation Act.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: charged expenditure under Article 113(1) can be discussed but not voted, yet it is still included in the Appropriation Act under Article 114 along with voted grants.

q: Flood damage on a division requires immediate restoration spending before Parliament can meet to authorise it. An advance for such unforeseen expenditure may be made from the Contingency Fund of India, which is placed at the disposal of:

options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

e: The Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of the President under Article 267, and advances for unforeseen expenditure like flood restoration are made from it.

q: Vouchers and accounts of field units are called for and examined at the headquarters office of the audit organisation, instead of a party visiting the unit. This mode of examination is known as:
e: Examination of vouchers and accounts at the headquarters office of the audit organisation, instead of by a visiting party at the unit, is central audit; visiting the unit is local audit.

q: A body receives a grant of Rs 30 lakh in a year, and that grant forms 80 per cent of its total expenditure for the year. Audit of such a substantially financed body by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is undertaken under which provision of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971?
e: A grant of Rs 30 lakh exceeds the Rs 25 lakh floor and 80 per cent exceeds the 75 per cent test, so the body is substantially financed and its audit falls under Section 14 of the DPC Act, 1971.

q: An executive proposes to meet a shortfall in a voted grant by transferring funds from a charged appropriation in the same section. The correct position is that re-appropriation:

options.A: Is not permissible from a charged appropriation to a voted grant, or vice versa
options.B: Is freely permissible within the same grant
options.C: Requires only the concurrence of the resident audit office
options.D: Can be ordered by the FA&CAO without restriction

e: Re-appropriation is not permissible from a charged appropriation to a voted grant, or vice versa, whatever the section, because the two rest on different constitutional authority.

q: A grant closes with an excess, though another grant of the same Ministry shows large savings. Before the excess can be regularised by an Excess Grant, it is first examined and its regularisation recommended by:

options.D: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

e: An excess over a grant is first examined by the Public Accounts Committee, and an Excess Grant is voted by Parliament only on the Committee's recommendation for regularisation.

q: During test audit, only a minor irregularity is noticed in a unit, not serious enough to call for a detailed Inspection Report. It is brought to the notice of the executive through:
e: A minor irregularity found in test audit, not serious enough for a detailed Inspection Report, is brought to the executive's notice through a Test Audit Note; Q714 states the same rule.

q: A works proposal with financial implications is put up for sanction. Under the system of associated finance followed on Railways, before the competent executive authority sanctions it, the proposal requires:

options.A: The concurrence of the associated finance, that is, the FA&CAO's organisation
options.B: The prior approval of the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: The certificate of the Principal Director of Audit
options.D: A vote of Parliament on a token demand

e: Under associated finance on Railways, a works proposal with financial implications requires the concurrence of the associated finance, the FA and CAO's organisation, before the executive authority sanctions it.

q: A zonal railway reports gross traffic earnings of Rs 2,500 crore and working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 2,250 crore. Its net revenue for the year is:
e: Net revenue = gross traffic earnings minus working expenses = Rs 2,500 crore - Rs 2,250 crore = Rs 250 crore.

q: A bridge asset has outlived the life prescribed for its class but is still in service and has not yet been renewed. In the Block Account of the Railway, the asset:

options.A: Is written off automatically on expiry of its prescribed life
options.B: Is revalued every year at current market price
options.C: Is transferred to the Public Account of India
options.D: Continues to be shown at its original capital cost until it is actually replaced or renewed

e: In the Railway Block Account, an asset continues to be shown at its original capital cost until it is actually replaced or renewed; expiry of its prescribed life alone does not write it off.

q: After the general discussion on the Union Budget is concluded, the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways are examined in detail, and a report on them submitted to the Houses, by:

options.C: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

e: After the general discussion, Railway Demands for Grants are examined in detail and reported on to the Houses by the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways.

q: The statutory auditors' report on a Government company is received by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. Within what period may he conduct a supplementary audit of the company's accounts under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: 30 days from receipt of the audit report
options.B: 60 days from receipt of the audit report
options.C: 90 days from receipt of the audit report
options.D: 120 days from receipt of the audit report

e: Under Section 143(6) of the Companies Act, 2013, the CAG may conduct a supplementary audit of a Government company within 60 days of receiving the statutory auditors' report; Q608 states the same period.

q: A competent authority accords a sanction involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India. Under the financial rules, a copy of the sanction is required to be communicated to:
e: Financial rules require every sanction to expenditure from the Consolidated Fund to be communicated to the Accounts Officer or Audit Officer concerned; Q620 states the same rule.

q: Heavy expenditure is incurred on a project which, owing to subsequent developments, is abandoned and fails to serve the purpose for which the money was spent. Audit terms such expenditure as:
e: Expenditure on a project that is abandoned and serves no purpose is infructuous expenditure - formally incurred but yielding no result, which audit brings to notice as a loss of public money.

q: A receipt cannot immediately be booked to its final head and is temporarily held under suspense pending clearance. In the Government system of classification, Suspense Accounts are grouped under Major Head:
e: Receipts held temporarily under suspense pending clearance are grouped under Major Head 8658, Suspense Accounts; Q701 states the same head.

q: The net revenue of a railway for a year is Rs 900 crore and its capital-at-charge is Rs 15,000 crore. The return on capital-at-charge works out to:
e: Return on capital-at-charge = net revenue divided by capital-at-charge x 100 = 900 / 15,000 x 100 = 6 per cent.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Accounts of the Union Government:
1. They are compiled by the accounting authorities of the Government, and not by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. They are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India after audit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct for the Union: since departmentalisation of accounts, the Finance Accounts are compiled by the Government's accounting authorities, not the CAG, and are certified by the CAG after audit.

q: In the budget documents, a guarantee given by the Government of India in respect of borrowings raised for a railway project is correctly shown as:

options.A: A part of the public debt of India
options.B: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: A deposit held in the Public Account of India
options.D: A contingent liability, which does not form part of the public debt

e: A Government guarantee is only a contingent liability: it involves no present debt and crystallises only on default, so it does not form part of the public debt of India.

q: Parliament is yet to complete the regular budget procedure, and the Lok Sabha makes grants in advance for a part of the financial year through a Vote on Account. Such a Vote on Account is normally taken for a period of:
e: A Vote on Account under Article 116(a) is normally taken for two months, covering the period until the regular Budget procedure is completed, though it can be longer in an election year.

q: Who was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of independent India?
e: V. Narahari Rao was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of independent India, holding the office from 1948 to 1954.

q: Under Article 322 of the Constitution, the expenses of one of the following bodies, including the salaries, allowances and pensions of its Chairman and members, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. That body is:
e: Article 322 charges the expenses of the Union Public Service Commission, including salaries, allowances and pensions of its Chairman and members, on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: House Building Advance granted to a Government servant is accounted for in the Government accounts under:

options.A: Revenue receipts of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The Loans and Advances section of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: House Building Advance is a loan given by Government, so it is accounted in the Loans and Advances section of the Consolidated Fund of India, under Major Head 7610 for Government servants.

q: Surveys and investigations are carried out at considerable cost for a new line project, but the project is ultimately abandoned. The cost of the surveys and investigations is charged to:
e: On Railways, the cost of surveys and investigations for a project that is ultimately abandoned is charged to Revenue, since no capital asset results from the spending.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings does not examine the accounts and reports of Indian Railways. The reason is that:

options.A: The accounts of Railways are treated as secret
options.B: Railways is audited by private firms of auditors
options.C: The Committee consists only of members of the Lok Sabha
options.D: Railways is a departmental undertaking of the Government, and not a public undertaking in the form of a company or corporation

e: The Committee on Public Undertakings does not examine Railways because Railways is a departmental undertaking of Government, not a public undertaking in company or corporation form; Q656 and Q699 state the same reason.

q: The accrual-based accounting standards being formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB) for Government accounts are known as:
e: The accrual-based standards formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board are the Indian Government Financial Reporting Standards, IGFRS; its cash-based standards are IGAS.

q: The Public Accounts Committee presents to Parliament reports recording the action taken by the Government on the Committee's earlier recommendations. These reports are known as:
e: Reports in which the Public Accounts Committee records the action taken by Government on its earlier recommendations are called Action Taken Reports; Q619 states the same term.

q: Under the systems-based approach to audit, the audit organisation places its main emphasis on:

options.A: Cent-per-cent substantive checking of all transactions
options.B: Checking only the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.C: Evaluating the system of internal control in the audited unit and directing the substantive test checks in the light of that evaluation
options.D: Auditing only the transactions pointed out by the executive

e: Systems-based audit places its main emphasis on evaluating the audited unit's internal control system and directing substantive test checks in the light of that evaluation; Q621 states the same approach.

q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha. The Rajya Sabha must return the Bill, with or without its recommendations, within a period of:
e: Under Article 109, the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha, with or without recommendations, within 14 days, failing which it is deemed passed by both Houses.

q:
Consider the following statements:
The documents laid before Parliament along with the Annual Financial Statement under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 include:
1. The Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement
2. The Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement
3. The Macro-economic Framework Statement
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: All three statements are correct: Section 3 of the FRBM Act, 2003 requires the Medium-term Fiscal Policy Statement, the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement and the Macro-economic Framework Statement to be laid with the Budget.
